freePlay.title: Free play
freePlay.intro: Play anything: the keys light up with their names, and chords and intervals are named as you play them.

progress.bestStreak: Best: {count, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}

skills.heading: Skills
skills.lessons: {played} of {total, plural, one {# lesson} other {# lessons}} played

activity.heading: Practice in the last year
activity.total: {time} on {count, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}
activity.empty: Each day you practice turns a square green.
activity.label: Practice per day over the last year

midi.heading: MIDI keyboard
midi.intro: Connect your digital piano to the computer with a USB cable, then enable MIDI.
midi.denied: MIDI access was blocked. Allow MIDI for this site in the browser’s site settings, then try again.
midi.unsupported: This browser doesn’t support MIDI. Use Chrome or Edge.
midi.noDevices: No MIDI devices found. Check the USB cable and that the keyboard is turned on.
midi.busy: Couldn’t open {device}. Another app may be using it: close other music software and try again.
midi.disconnected: {device} is disconnected. It will reconnect automatically when it’s plugged back in.

devKeyboard.heading: Computer keyboard
devKeyboard.enable: Use the computer keyboard as a piano
devKeyboard.help: Keys A W S E D F T G Y H U J K play one octave, from {note} to the next {note}. Z and X change the octave.
devKeyboard.sound: Play a piano sound for the computer and on-screen keyboards
devKeyboard.slowOutput: That’s a noticeable delay, usually caused by Bluetooth headphones or speakers. Wired headphones or speakers respond much faster.

liveTest.heading: Live test
liveTest.intro: Press keys on your piano. Each one should appear here, with the right name.

hints.auto: Uses the MIDI keyboard when it’s connected, otherwise the microphone.
hints.midi: Only notes from the MIDI keyboard count.
hints.mic: Only notes the microphone hears count. Use this for an acoustic piano.

listening.none: Not listening to an instrument yet: connect a MIDI keyboard or turn on the microphone.
listening.midiOff: The MIDI keyboard isn’t connected. Enable MIDI below.
listening.micOff: The microphone is off. Turn it on below.

mic.heading: Microphone
mic.intro: Place the microphone near the piano. It hears one note at a time; chords come later.
mic.unsupported: This browser can’t use the microphone. Use Chrome or Edge.
mic.denied: Microphone access was blocked. Allow it for this site in the browser’s site settings, then try again.
mic.error: The microphone couldn’t start. Check that it’s connected and not used by another app.
mic.thresholdHint: Lower it if soft notes are missed; raise it if noise is detected as notes.
mic.summary: Background noise: {noise} dB · Delay correction: {delay} ms
mic.headphones: To measure the delay, play any key on each click. Headphones help, so the microphone doesn’t hear the clicks.
mic.delayRunning: Play a key on each click: {beat} of {total}
mic.delayDone: Delay correction set to {ms} ms ({taps} of {total} clicks heard).
mic.failed: That didn’t work: not enough was heard. Try again, playing a little louder.

micCheck.heading: Microphone check
micCheck.intro: With both the MIDI cable and the microphone on, play notes across the keyboard. MIDI says which keys you really played, so this shows how well the microphone hears them.
micCheck.record: Record the audio, to help improve note detection
micCheck.saveHint: Saves one file (.json) with the microphone audio and the notes you played on MIDI. Put it in the project’s fixtures/mic folder.

sound.heading: Sound and timing
sound.intro: If the metronome clicks sound late (or early) compared with the falling notes, measure the timing: tap any key on your piano exactly with each click.
sound.running: Tap a key exactly with each click: {beat} of {total}
sound.done: Clicks now play {ms} ms earlier ({taps} of {total} taps used).
sound.failed: Not enough taps were heard. Try again, tapping a key on every click.
sound.micFirst: Do this before measuring the microphone delay.

practice.hint: Play each note when it reaches the keyboard. The metronome counts you in.
practice.hintWait: The music waits for you: play the highlighted keys to continue.

timing.heading: Timing
timing.chart: When each note was played: {early} early, {onTime} on time, {late} late
timing.average: {direction, select, early {On average {ms} ms early} late {On average {ms} ms late} other {On average right on the beat}}

bars.heading: Bar by bar
bars.hint: Click a bar to repeat it.

practice.sheetError: Couldn’t show the sheet music. Try falling notes instead.

loop.label: Repeat bars
loop.tip: Tip: drag across bars on the music to repeat them.
loop.hint: The chosen bars repeat until you stop.
loop.lastPass: {count, plural, one {Once through} other {# times through}} · last time {accuracy}

practice.otherHandMic: With the microphone, use headphones so it only hears you.

lesson.allFound: Well done! You found them all.
lesson.passRule: {stars, plural, one {Earn # star to pass} other {Earn # stars to pass}}
lesson.noStars: Finish every step without skipping to earn stars.
lesson.bestStars: {stars, plural, one {Your best: # star} other {Your best: # stars}}

language.heading: Language and note names
language.intro: Choose your language, and how notes should be named: letters ({letters}) or solfège ({solfege}).

instrument.heading: Your instrument
instrument.intro: Connect a digital piano with a USB cable, or use the microphone with an acoustic piano. You can also play with the computer keyboard.

test.heading: Try it
test.intro: Press a few keys. Each one should appear below with its name. You can change all of this later in Settings.
